response.query: What is our primary TFP measure and estimation method, and which alternative specifications (OP/LP/ACF, region-aggregated vs micro) and selection corrections will be pre-registered for robustness?
response.answer: Our primary TFP measure uses the Levinsohn-Petrin method. Alternative specifications include OP and LP methods. Pre-registration for robustness includes region-aggregated vs micro data and selection corrections.

results.content: I know there are issues concerning the elasticity of substitution within the COGS inputs, prices etc - but I'm wondering in general about production function estimation without using a particular variable as a productivity proxy. I will try to answer your questions below: 1) At the moment, _prodest_ does not directly implement DLEU model - nor DLW (2013), which if I am not mistaken is the paper in which the method was originally developed. If I could ask a follow-up question: when you say that _prodest_ does not implement the DLEU or DLW approach but it is close, I just wanted to confirm as to what the differences are you refer to. I see the following, but wanted to check if I had missed anything: 1) DLEU use the same variable for the free input and as the proxy; this is not the case for ACF or _prodest_. 2) DLEU and DLW suggest a process for productivity which is more general than AR(1) (though in DLW's mock code they do actually use an AR(1) process); ACF suggest an AR(1) process and this is what is used in _prodest_. Below I will address the questions you raised: 1) Correct, that is one of the most controversial aspects of DLEU; 2) Again, all correct - but I'd follow DLW in using an AR(1) process (moreover, that is what is actually already implemented in _prodest_) ; 3) I am not sure to get the point.
